subtype: Approach: asking the teacher to pair him with a buddy [Action]
passage:
Monday. Vinay stood in the corridor of his new school, clutching his bag. He did not know where the canteen was, or the library, or even where to turn. At the end of the day he went to Leela Ma'am's desk. "I don't know where things are, ma'am."

Tuesday. Leela Ma'am smiled. "This is Vandana. She'll show you around." Vandana pointed out the canteen, the library and the water tank.

Friday. Vinay walked to the library alone and found the shelf he wanted. "Thanks, Vandana," he said at lunch. She shrugged, and pushed over her tiffin for him to share.

qa.q: Who showed Vinay around the school?
qa.a: Vandana showed Vinay around the school.

qa.q: What was Vinay feeling in the corridor on Monday?
qa.a: Vinay was probably lost and anxious, clutching his bag because he did not know where anything was.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Vinay use, and why?
qa.a: Vinay could ask another classmate or check a school map, but a named buddy gives regular help and friendly company.

qa.q: How might Vandana see being asked to show Vinay around?
qa.a: Vandana pointed out the places and later shared her tiffin, so Vandana probably found it easy and friendly, and possibly gained a new friend.

grounding: A new student tells the teacher he does not know where things are, and the teacher pairs him with a classmate who shows him the canteen, library and water tank.

subtype: Approach: asking the teacher to pair him with a buddy [Action]
passage: Vaibhav, you're nervous about the new school, so let your Gurpreet Dadi tell you about a boy I taught, long ago. His name was Ronak. On his first day he came to my desk after the bell, very red in the face, and said, "Ma'am, I don't know where anything is. I got lost looking for the toilet." Most children never say that. They wander around feeling foolish. So I called Iqbal, the friendliest boy in my class, and said, "Ronak is your buddy this week. Show him the canteen, the library and the toilets." By lunch they were eating together. By Friday Ronak was showing another new child where the library was. It began because he asked.

qa.q: What had Ronak got lost looking for?
qa.a: He got lost looking for the toilet.

qa.q: How was Ronak feeling when he came to the teacher's desk?
qa.a: He was embarrassed and anxious, red in the face, but brave enough to ask.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Ronak's first week, and what else could he have done?
qa.a: The turning point was telling the teacher he felt lost; he could also have asked a classmate directly, but asking the teacher got him a buddy for the whole week.

qa.q: How might Iqbal have seen being made Ronak's buddy?
qa.a: Iqbal was probably proud to be trusted with the job and happy to have someone new to eat lunch with.

grounding: An elder recalls a new student telling the teacher he did not know his way around, and the teacher pairing him with a friendly classmate.

passage: Abhinav's first day at the big school in Bengaluru was a wet one. Rain drummed on the corridors, and half the building was fenced off for repairs, so even old students were taking odd routes. After assembly Abhinav stood in the crowd, lost. He found his class teacher at the staffroom door. "Nikita ma'am, I don't know where the canteen or the library is, and the signs are covered." She nodded. "Good that you told me." She waved over a girl with an umbrella. "Meher, will you take Abhinav round today? Canteen, library, toilets, and the new way to the ground." Meher showed him the shortcut past the repair fence. By the second bell, Abhinav had his own map in his head.

qa.q: Why were even old students taking odd routes?
qa.a: Half the building was fenced off for repairs.

qa.q: How did Abhinav feel standing lost after assembly?
qa.a: He felt confused and worried in the crowd, with the signs covered and the building changed.

qa.q: What else could Abhinav do if Meher was busy the next day?
qa.a: He could draw a small map in his diary of the routes she showed him, so he can find his own way.

qa.q: How does the request look to Nikita ma'am?
qa.a: Nikita ma'am is glad he told her and sees an easy fix, pairing him with a helpful classmate.

grounding: It shows a new student telling his teacher he does not know his way around, and the teacher assigning a classmate to show him the key places.
